paper.core_task: Robust distributed learning with Byzantine workers using adaptive gradient clipping

contributions.name: Adaptive robust clipping scheme for distributed learning
contributions.author_claim_text: We propose ARC, wherein prior to aggregating the gradients, the server clips the largest k := ⌊2(f /n)(n -f )⌋ gradients using a clipping parameter given by the (Euclidean) norm of the (k + 1)-th largest gradient.
contributions.description: Introduces an adaptive pre-aggregation clipping method that dynamically sets the clipping threshold based on the norm of a ranked gradient and the fraction of adversarial workers.

contributions.name: Robustness preservation guarantee for adaptive clipping
contributions.author_claim_text: We prove that ARC preserves the robustness guarantee of the original robust aggregation method.
contributions.description: Demonstrates that composing an existing robust aggregation method with ARC maintains its (f, κ)-robustness property, with a bounded increase in the robustness coefficient.

contributions.name: Improved convergence guarantee under good initialization
contributions.author_claim_text: When the model initialization is good, ARC provably improves the robustness of Robust-DGD.
contributions.description: Shows that ARC can achieve a lower stationarity error than the known lower bound when honest worker gradients are small at initialization, effectively increasing the system's breakdown point.

novelty_claims.text: The proposed adaptive clipping scheme is similar to the one proposed in Diakonikolas et al. (2020).
